liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lazy Lightnin'** (3 reviews): Gives a nod to Lazy Lightnin' into Supplication; Phil shines especially during Lazy Lightnin' [12][14][15]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Brent's playing in Fire feels watery, with Jerry's playing steady alongside; interesting jams in Scarlet>Fire; The next-to-last break in Fire is praised as outstanding [15][22]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Suggests Let It Grow may be a top-10 version; The end of Let It Grow unravels wonderfully [20][22]
- **Deal** (1 review): Sound quality worsens near the end of the rave-up Deal [14]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Singles out the Scarlet>Fire>Let It Grow sequence, plus a strong jam after Let It Grow [12]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' into Wharf Rat is called ridiculously good [20]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Calls Wharf Rat excellent and the drums/space segment hot [12]
- **Don't Ease Me In** (1 review): Don't Ease Me In is called one of the best ever [22]

## The recordings

- **gd79-12-30.rolfe.vernon.18221.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 138 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has Garcia low in the mix at times, while Weir is prominent [14]
- **gd1979-12-30.sbd.ladner.tetzeli.fix-4797.35219.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 131 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1979-12-30.167451.nak700.biggar.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 140 min [3]
- **gd1979-12-30.154880.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 134 min [5]
- **gd1979-12-30.sonyecm.severson.minches.90677.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [9]
- **gd1979-12-30.senn421.walker-scotton.miller.89259.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 138 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [10]. Said about its sound: This audience recording sounds lively, unlike soundboards from the run that feel somewhat sterile despite precision [23]
- **gd79-12-30.sbd.ladner.4797.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 131 min; rated 4.27/5 by 11 [11]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended amid Iran hostage tensions, feared it might be the band's last chance, and brought his wife, who got it [13]
- Purple gels dominated the stage lighting that night [17]
- Short Sunday concert; hall was not too crowded, and reviewer went home exhausted and missed the next night [19]
- Bob Weir was sick at this show, as also on the next night, New Year's [21]
- Reviewer says the venue's acoustics sound really good [23]
- Considers the show short and to the point, which they see as a good thing [13]
- Show stands out as unusual for its timing, right in the middle of a run [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-12-30.rolfe.vernon.18221.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Taped by Steve Rolfe on Nak 700s into a D5, then DAT, via Dave Minor; encoded by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1979-12-30.sbd.ladner.tetzeli.fix-4797.35219.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller & Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD>MC>DAT>CD [2]. Also: Soundboard was patched with an audience source from LlaMA, with the patch from end of space to end of Truckin' redone [2]
- **gd1979-12-30.167451.nak700.biggar.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by David Biggar; transferred by Matt Smith, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Master 1/2 Track Audience Reels; Nakamichi 700 mics (mounted on a 30' pole) > Technics RS-1500 Reel to Reel @ 7 1/2 ips (DBX encoded) > DBX224 > 1st generation… [3]
- **gd1979-12-30.154880.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [5]. Also: Source cassettes and transfer by Scott Wiseman, with Sennheiser 421 patches in Supplication, Deal, Scarlet>Fire, Let It Grow and Drums [5]
- **gd1979-12-30.sonyecm.severson.minches.90677.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by David Minches; source: 2 Sony ECM-270s on stand 35' from stage> Sony TC-D5 (2 Maxell UD XL-IIs) [9]. Also: Recording was made by Mark Severson of Seattle, known to the reviewer as an excellent taper [21]
- **gd1979-12-30.senn421.walker-scotton.miller.89259.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-II90) [10]
- **gd79-12-30.sbd.ladner.4797.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [11]. Also: Their first tape of the show had Truckin' replaced by an audience version, decent but somewhat distracting; Reviewer downloaded the board recording before it was removed; an audience recording remains available [13][17]
